repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
wait until(all(#TemperatureSensor).temperatureSensor_temperature < 30)
triggered = false
}
wait until(all(#TemperatureSensor).temperatureSensor_temperature >= 30)
all(#WindowCovering).windowCovering_downOrClose()
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The candidate polls the condition only at the start of the 1-second cycle period. The IR requires a rising-edge wait, which must block until the condition transitions from false to true. Evidence F2 shows the action was missed at 100ms because the candidate's `if` evaluated to false (condition was just becoming true, not yet true at the previous sample), failing to trigger the rising edge logic.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` polling with a blocking two-wait rising-edge state machine. The script now blocks on `wait until(P == false)` if previously triggered, then blocks on `wait until(P == true)` to catch the rising edge, executes the action, and sets the flag. This preserves the 1-second cycle period for re-arming while ensuring the action fires exactly at the rising edge.
